tools.description: Discover command ids, labels, parameter descriptions and enabled state. Returns an array. The whole catalogue is large: narrow it with filter (or query), menu, and brief.

brief.description: Leave out each command's params description (the bulk of the catalogue); run command_list with the id as filter to read it

filter.description: Case-insensitive id, label or menu substring

menu.description: Case-insensitive substring of the menu path, its levels joined with " > " (e.g. "Object", "Object > Path")

tools.name: command_list

tools.description: Run an engine command by id with its JSON params. Command parameters follow the registry's descriptions.
tools.name: command_run
tools.title: Run a command

tools.description: Run steps in order; each edit is its own undo step, or with atomic:true the whole batch is one (named `label`, else after its first edit). A step's id is a command id, or draw_path / draw_shape with that tool's arguments as params (its result is the tool's: the new object's `id`). A param string that is exactly "$N.path" (N: 0-based step index) or "$last.path" takes that value from an earlier step's result, e.g. {"id":"$1.id"}; "$$" starts a literal "$". Returns completed, failed, results and created (the ids draw_path / draw_shape steps made, in order). Stops on the first error by default. At most 256 steps; kept step results total at most 8 MiB, past which the batch stops with the reason.

atomic.description: Make the batch's edits one undo step (needs an open document)

label.description: The undo step's name with atomic

tools.name: command_batch
tools.title: Run several commands

tools.description: Summary of the active document, including artboards, layer tree, selection and history. On a large document scope it: depth 0 for the layer skeleton, ids for just those nodes, kind for every node of one kind, limit/offset to page.

kind.description: List every node of this panel label (Layer, Group, Path, Type, Image, ...; ignores case) as `nodes`, each with its ancestor `path`; searches the subtrees of `ids` when given

limit.description: At most this many layers or nodes (the reply adds `total`)

Omitted paint fields inherit the current new-art appearance (initially white fill and 1 pt black stroke). For a filled path without an outline, pass an explicit fill and stroke:"none". Returns the new object id.

Omitted paint fields inherit the current new-art appearance (initially white fill and 1 pt black stroke); lines start with no fill and a visible stroke. For a filled shape without an outline, pass an explicit fill and stroke:"none". Stroke dash/cap/join, opacity, name and live effects apply to the new shape as in draw_path. Returns the new object id.

tools.description: Open a file as a new, active document: .vectorcraft, .drawcraft, .svg, .svgz, .pdf, .ai, .ait, .png, .jpg, .jpeg, .gif, .webp, .tif, .tiff, .bmp, .psd, .psb, .vctemplate, .dxf, .emf, .wmf, .eps, .epsf, .ps, .af, .afdesign, .afpub (see run_command document.formats). Templates (.ait, native templates) open as a new untitled document. The reply's `warnings` say what didn't come in as it was (an EPS shown as its preview image says why its PostScript couldn't be read).
tools.name: open_file
tools.title: Open file

tools.description: Save the active document with the engine's document.save: by default to its own file in its own format (native .vectorcraft unless it was opened from or saved as SVG, PDF or a restorable .ai). With `path`, the extension picks the format: .vectorcraft, .vctemplate, .pdf, .svg, .svgz, .ai. Other formats are exports (see export). The reply's `format` says what was written and `warnings` what that format loses.

path.description: Destination; its extension picks the format (default: the document's own file)

tools.name: save_file
tools.title: Save file

tools.description: Export the active document with the engine's document.export (the same bytes in the app and headless), in any format of the `format` enum: vectors (svg/svgz with the artboard as viewBox, eps, dxf, emf, wmf), pdf and ai (one page per artboard: all, or `artboard` / `range`; ai is the PDF-compatible .ai file that Save writes, which carries the document when every artboard is written in order), rasters (one rendered artboard: png, jpg, webp, gif, png8 as an indexed .png, tiff, bmp, tga, psd with its layers), txt (the stories, back to front), vectorcraft or template (a native copy or template; the document keeps its path). run_command document.formats lists each format's options. For SVG/SVGZ, top-level `outlineText: true` writes text as paths; DXF takes it too (its type is outlined anyway unless `preserve: editability`). PDF instead uses `options.advanced.outlineText: true`, default false (live text). `selection: true` exports only the selected objects, cropped to their bounds. Template layers are left out; live effects are kept (geometry baked, SVG filters for shadows/glows/blur). Without `path` the bytes come back as dataBase64.

artboard.description: 0-based artboard (default: the first; PDF and .ai default: all)

options.description: More format options, passed through (see run_command document.formats), e.g. {"quality": 80} for jpg or {"advanced": {"outlineText": true}} for PDF text as outlines (default false: live text)

outlineText.description: SVG/SVGZ: true writes text as outlines (viewable without the fonts). DXF takes it too (type outlined anyway unless preserve: editability). PDF uses options.advanced.outlineText instead (default false: live text)

range.description: 1-based artboards such as "1-3, 5" (PDF and .ai: one page each; SVG, SVGZ and EPS: one file each; rasters, DXF, EMF and WMF: one, or one file each with options.useArtboards: true)

selection.description: Export only the selection, cropped to it

Returns the text object id, with `overflow: true` when the text doesn't fit its frame or path (the lines past it aren't drawn: enlarge the frame, shrink the text or give `fit`).

color.description: Text colour (#rrggbb): "#rrggbb", "none", [r,g,b] (0..1), {"c","m","y","k"}, {"gray"}, or a full paint.setFill params object ({"gradient":…} / {"swatch":name})

path.description: Existing path id to flow the text in (area) or along (onPath)

vertical.description: Vertical writing for point, area or path type (default false, horizontal), as text.create / text.createInPath

x.description: Baseline origin x (area type: left; point type: where the line starts, or its centre or end with justify center/right)
